summary: Martian Map is an interactive prototype for planning and simulating a walk in Mars’s Gale Crater. It combines NASA orbital imagery, a THEMIS infrared layer, and terrain elevation in one map. Users choose a starting point and destinations, then explore a proposed route with estimates of distance, slope, travel time, and oxygen use. The analysis includes a return to the starting point and flags destinations that exceed the model’s terrain or oxygen limits. During a simulated walk, a dashboard shows the astronaut’s progress and displays resource and route alerts. Martian Map addresses the challenge by bringing scattered Mars data together in a tool that helps explorers assess a route before setting out and keep the journey home in view.
details:
Martian Map is a web prototype that helps users plan and simulate a walk in Mars’s Gale Crater. Its layered map brings together NASA Mars imagery, terrain elevation, and a THEMIS infrared layer. Users select a starting point and up to six places to visit. The route analysis estimates distance, elevation change, travel time, and oxygen use, then checks whether the planned journey can return to its starting point with an oxygen reserve. It identifies destinations that cannot be included under the model’s terrain or oxygen limits.

After planning, users can follow the route in a simulated walk. A dashboard updates the astronaut’s position and shows oxygen estimates, the cost of returning, and alerts. For demonstrations, a phone can act as a controller. The astronaut’s movement and vital signs are simulated; the project does not use a physical spacesuit or live medical sensors.

We developed the interface with JavaScript, React, Vite, OpenLayers, and proj4. Node.js and Express connect the interface to backend services, while Python handles terrain and route analysis using imagery and elevation data. The project’s creative approach is to connect route planning with the experience of carrying out the walk: users can see how a decision made on the map affects the journey and the ability to return.

Our team considered steep and rough terrain, incomplete elevation coverage, limited oxygen, and the need to make warnings easy to understand. The intended impact is to make Mars exploration data easier to use when evaluating a traverse. Martian Map is an exploratory prototype; its estimates would need further validation before use in a real mission.
